name: Earth
blurb: Hot gas rises, so flames stretch into a teardrop and pull in fresh air. Every ground flammability test happens here.

name: International Space Station
blurb: No buoyancy. Flames turn round, dim and slow, and feed on oxygen by diffusion and cabin ventilation. Almost all NASA combustion data was taken here.

name: Spacesuit (EVA)
basis: Team scenario: pure oxygen at 4.3 psi
blurb: Pure oxygen at low pressure. Far outside anything in the microgravity tables.

name: Moon base
blurb: Richer oxygen at lower pressure to shorten spacewalk preparation. One-sixth gravity sits between the two regimes that were tested.

name: Pressurized rover
basis: Assumed NASA exploration atmosphere (8.2 psi, 34% O2). Verify before citing.
blurb: Small sealed cabin with frequent spacewalks. Higher oxygen fraction than any habitat flown so far.

name: Mars habitat
basis: Assumed NASA exploration atmosphere (8.2 psi, 34% O2). Verify before citing.
blurb: About three-eighths gravity. No rescue and no resupply for months, so prevention matters most.
